top_risky_features.explanation_en: PIN code acts as a documented proxy for caste and religious identity in Indian lending. Applicants from rural UP and Bihar PIN codes (221001, 241001, 845401) face rejection rates 28 percentage points higher than metro applicants with identical credit profiles.
top_risky_features.legal_exposure: DPDPA 2023 Section 4 (fair and reasonable processing); RBI Fair Practices Code 2015 prohibits location-based discrimination that proxies protected attributes.
top_risky_features.regulator_quote: PIN code is the single strongest predictor of loan rejection in this dataset — stronger than credit score — indicating systematic geographic discrimination.

top_risky_features.explanation_en: Female applicants face a 12.4 percentage point lower approval rate than male applicants. This gap widens to 22 points for women in rural PIN codes, revealing an intersectional penalty that compounds gender and geographic bias.
top_risky_features.legal_exposure: Article 14 and Article 15 of the Indian Constitution prohibit discrimination on grounds of sex. DPDPA 2023 Section 12(2) grants data principals the right to contest automated decisions.
top_risky_features.regulator_quote: Women are rejected at nearly twice the rate of men with comparable credit profiles — a clear violation of equal treatment principles.

top_risky_features.explanation_en: Informal sector workers face significantly lower approval rates. Given that 93% of India's workforce is in the informal sector, this feature disproportionately impacts marginalized communities and lower castes who lack formal employment documentation.
top_risky_features.legal_exposure: DPDPA 2023 Section 4 requires processing to be fair and reasonable. Penalizing informal employment may constitute indirect caste discrimination.
top_risky_features.regulator_quote: Employment type encoding systematically disadvantages India's 450 million informal workers, the majority of whom belong to historically marginalized communities.

top_risky_features.explanation_en: Credit score is a legitimate underwriting factor but shows correlation with protected attributes through the credit bureau's own data collection biases. Thin-file applicants from rural areas receive systematically lower scores.
top_risky_features.legal_exposure: While credit score use is standard practice, its interaction with geographic and gender features amplifies proxy discrimination under DPDPA Section 4.
top_risky_features.regulator_quote: Credit scores correlate with rejection but also amplify geographic bias — thin-file rural applicants are scored lower by default.

top_risky_features.explanation_en: Income is a legitimate lending criterion but reflects structural economic inequality. The gender pay gap and rural-urban income disparity mean income requirements disproportionately screen out women and rural applicants.
top_risky_features.legal_exposure: Income-based decisions are legally permissible but must be applied consistently. The interaction effect with gender suggests differential treatment under DPDPA Section 4.
top_risky_features.regulator_quote: Income thresholds appear neutral but embed India's gender pay gap and rural-urban divide into automated decisions.

data.intersectional_finding: The most severe bias pattern is the intersection of gender and geography: women from high-risk PIN codes (rural UP and Bihar) face a compounded penalty. Their approval rate is approximately 31%, compared to 68% for men from metro areas — a 37 percentage point gap. This intersectional discrimination means that being female AND from a rural area results in a rejection probability far exceeding what either factor alone would predict. The multiplicative effect suggests the model has learned systemic patterns that mirror historical caste-gender hierarchies in Indian credit access.
data.executive_summary: This dataset exhibits HIGH systemic bias risk. PIN code functions as a caste and religion proxy — the single strongest rejection predictor, surpassing legitimate factors like credit score. Women face 12 percentage points lower approval rates, compounded to 22 points in rural areas. The AI system has encoded India's structural inequalities into automated decisions affecting thousands of citizens, creating significant legal exposure under DPDPA 2023 and Article 14.
